newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore condemns Cambodian violence, urges peace.
newsitem.headline: Singapore condemns Cambodian violence, urges peace.

text.p: Singapore called on Sunday for all parties in Cambodia to cease military activities, and condemned the use of violent means to change government.
Intense fighting has rocked the Cambodian capital Phnom Penh for the last two days as troops loyal to First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh battle those of Second Prime Minister Hun Sen.
"The Singapore government is deeply concerned about the deterioration of the situation in Cambodia," a statement issued by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MFA) said.
It called on all parties involved "to exercise utmost restraint, cease military activities and restore calm to the country."
"Singapore disapproves of the change of government through violent means and calls on all parties to adhere to the constitutional processes in place in Cambodia."
The statement also said Singapore's embassy in Phnom Penh had advised Singaporeans resident in Cambodia to remain indoors for the present.

At least 12 people have died and more than 50 have been wounded in the fighting. A Japanese man who died in Phnom Penh on Sunday was the only foreign casualty reported thus far but details on the identities of the dead and wounded are sketchy.
